BOUNDARY:  
The block estimate is trivial when \(p=q\); the denominator \(\iota(p+1)\) is never zero. The weighted estimates are checked at the extreme \(x_N=0\) (which forces \(N=0\) and gives \(1-x_N^n=0\) for \(n=0\) and \(x_N^n=0\) for \(n>0\), satisfying the inequalities). For large \(N\), \(x_N\to1\) and the product \(x_N^{N+1}\frac{\iota(N+1)}{\iota(N+2)}\) remains \(<1\) because \(x_N^{N+1}\le 1\) and \(\iota(N+1)/\iota(N+2)<1\). The infinite tail sum converges by comparison with a convergent geometric series (\(|x_N|<1\)). The bound \(\sum_{n>N}|a_n|x_N^n\) is therefore well-defined.
